# Embabel RAG Graph

> Graph-backed RAG for the Embabel Agent Framework: chunk, section and document storage with vector
> and full-text search on Neo4j, FalkorDB, Memgraph, Oracle and Postgres, through Drivine.

## Rules for changing this code

- Go through Drivine's `StatelessGraphObjectManager` first: `@NodeFragment` models, `@GraphView`s and
  the generated query DSL (`gom.loadAll`, `gom.saveAll`, `gom.delete`). Drivine writes the Cypher for
  the configured engine, SQL/PGQ on Oracle and plain SQL on Postgres, so the same model runs on Neo4j,
  FalkorDB, Memgraph, Oracle and Postgres.
- Oracle and Postgres do not run Cypher. A hand-written Cypher statement needs another way there, through the
  object manager.
- A chunk loaded from the store carries a stamp (`@NodeStamp`). To change a loaded chunk and write it
  back, use `gom.save`, which is refused when the chunk changed meanwhile. `saveAll` does not compare
  stamps.
- Do not copy the hand-written Cypher that exists elsewhere in this repository as a pattern for
  `GraphObjectManagerStore`. Write Cypher there only when the object manager has no reasonable way
  to say it, for features or for speed, and say why at the site.
- When Drivine cannot express something, prefer adding the feature to Drivine
  (https://github.com/liberation-data/drivine4j) over working around it here.
- Order by a property only with a range index that mirrors the ordering. Drivine's index advisor
  warns when none does.
- Put each `@NodeFragment` and `@GraphView` in its own file under `graph/model`.
- A change must pass on all five engines. The cross-engine suite is
  `AbstractRagSearchCharacterizationTest` and its Neo4j, FalkorDB, Memgraph, Oracle and Postgres
  subclasses. The Oracle and Postgres ones run in a plain `mvn test`.

## Where things are

- [README](README.md): supported databases, usage (with Oracle and Postgres), how the store works, and testing.
- `src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/rag/graph/GraphObjectManagerStore.kt`: the store.
- `src/main/kotlin/com/embabel/agent/rag/graph/model/`: fragments and views.
